source_snapshot.procedure: Master sends OEM `ipmitool raw 0x30 0x21 0x00` and checks every fan speed.
source_snapshot.criteria: Fan speed in SDR should be 20%; `0h = Auto Control (follow fan control algorithm)`.
source_snapshot.deepseek: PARTIAL substitutes OEM `0x30 0x30 0x01 0x01`, then greps fan sensors. It has no authoritative state decoder, complete topology, thermal watchdog, bounded observation or recovery if the supposed restore command fails, and it exposes credentials in arguments.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION correctly treats auto restoration as CRITICAL and requires vendor command resolution, explicit approval, state proof, closed-loop behavior and thermal monitoring.

old_problem: The Master and DeepSeek propose different vendor raw commands, while the Criterion simultaneously describes temperature-driven auto control and mandates a fixed 20-percent output. A single instantaneous 20-percent reading or successful completion code cannot prove controller state or feedback behavior. The exact restore and readback semantics are core, safety-critical unknowns.
disposition_reason: ED-03 forbids selecting or composing undocumented OEM bytes, and no public IPMI standard defines these command payloads. The adjacent manual and Get cases repeat incompatible command families rather than resolving them. Because this case is the mandatory recovery from a potentially unsafe manual override, it cannot be parameterized as an arbitrary runtime command: the owner must approve exact restore/readback behavior and resolve whether 20 percent is a minimum, an instantaneous example, a display convention or an erroneous fixed criterion.
decision_basis: XLSX row 977, same-row DeepSeek, exact GPT V2, tests JSON, selection manifest, historical V3.1 record and adjacent row 978 were directly reviewed; next pending was verified as Functionality row 978 / variant abbc6c7135373d90.
IPMI v2.0 leaves OEM command meaning to the manufacturer/product implementation; it cannot establish `0x30/0x21/0x00` or `0x30/0x30/0x01/0x01` as the correct auto command for this BMC firmware.

Automatic fan control is a controller mode with feedback behavior. Its duty may equal 20 percent at one operating point, but a fixed value is not generally equivalent to following a temperature-dependent algorithm.

The next Get case introduces a third Master read command (`0x30 0x22`) and another DeepSeek raw family (`0x30 0x30 0x01 0x02`); neither is an approved independent state readback until vendor semantics are supplied.

ED-03, ED-05, ED-14, ED-15, ED-16, ED-17, ED-19, ED-21 and ED-30 require authoritative command/expected result, safe recovery and preserved coverage; ED-34 through ED-38 require approved tools, explicit per-run confirmation, bounded monitoring and no automatic retry.

test_case.test_name: Restore and prove automatic closed-loop fan control after a known manual override
test_case.purpose: Under explicit authorization, execute the exact vendor-approved transition from a verified manual override to automatic fan control, prove the resulting mode through an independent authoritative state signal and bounded temperature-dependent fan behavior across every mapped channel, and leave no residual override or thermal alarm; do not treat a coincidental 20-percent reading as sufficient proof.
required_package: Vendor/platform-owner command specification tied to exact BMC manufacturer/product/model/firmware defining the auto-mode command, response/completion codes and idempotency behavior
Independent approved read-only control-mode and duty query/decoder that does not merely repeat the write command's acknowledgement
Owner disposition of the fixed 20-percent Criterion: required minimum, expected initial point with tolerance/context, display encoding or source defect
Verified precondition establishing the current manual/override mode and complete controller-to-fan/rotor/sensor topology
Approved observation interval, safe temperature/RPM/health/alarm limits, minimum evidence of closed-loop response, watchdog timeout and incident recovery/escalation runbook
Pinned reviewed Script content, secret-safe authenticated execution, preserved logs and explicit per-run user authorization
test_case.test_command: DO NOT EXECUTE while Pending. After authoritative command/state semantics and the 20-percent rule are approved: verify immutable target/manufacturer/product/firmware and a genuine manual-override precondition; preserve control mode/duty, complete mapped RPM/temperature/health/alarm and SEL/audit baseline. Arm independent monitoring, timeout and staffed abort. With explicit per-run approval, issue exactly one approved auto-mode command through a secret-safe path. Decode its completion response, query mode/duty through the independent approved interface, and observe every mapped fan and relevant temperature over the approved interval to demonstrate automatic feedback behavior under the owner-approved non-destructive context. Confirm the resolved 20-percent criterion only as specified, not by assumption. Stop on session loss, stale/missing telemetry, fan stall, temperature rise, alarm or unverified mode. Preserve final state/logs; do not clear logs, send alternate raw bytes, automatically retry or leave manual override active.
test_case.expected_result: The exact intended controller transitions from the verified manual state to the authoritative Auto state, independent readback reports the approved Auto encoding, no override remains, and every mapped fan exhibits safe behavior consistent with the approved closed-loop evidence model over the observation interval. The resolved 20-percent expectation is satisfied in its approved context, temperatures/health/alarms remain acceptable, logs contain no unexpected fan-control event, and final state is safe.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires a model/firmware-bound approved auto command, independent state decoder, verified manual precondition, explicit per-run approval, complete fan topology, resolved 20-percent semantics, bounded closed-loop behavior proof, thermal watchdog and healthy final logs/state. Completion-code success, one SDR value, a grepped fan list, read-only Get without the transition or a fixed 20-percent coincidence cannot pass. Wrong/ambiguous command, absent state proof, residual override, missing/stale fan data, unsafe RPM/temperature/alarm or unresolved Criterion is FAIL/NOT READY. Until command and acceptance authority exists, this remains ENGINEERING DECISION PENDING.
safety_gate: Never execute during review or select between Master and DeepSeek raw bytes without model/firmware-specific vendor approval.
Require a verified manual-override precondition, exact target identity, secret-safe credentials, explicit per-run confirmation and staffed abort ownership.
Arm independent full fan/temperature/health/alarm monitoring and a bounded timeout before the state change; monitoring loss is an abort, not a reason to continue.
Prove Auto with an authoritative independent mode query and approved closed-loop behavior; do not equate command acknowledgement or one 20-percent duty with recovered feedback control.
If Auto cannot be proven, invoke only the approved incident path; do not try alternate guessed commands, power-cycle or automatically retry.
Preserve pre/during/post logs and evidence; do not clear logs, expose credentials, reduce the case to passive telemetry or claim recovery while override status is unknown.
expected_evidence: Owner-approved auto command and independent state decoder tied to BMC identity/firmware, resolved 20-percent interpretation and pinned Script review
Explicit per-run approval and baseline proof of manual mode with complete mapped RPM, temperature, health, alarms and preserved logs
Exact command metadata/response, decoded independent control-mode/duty readback and timestamps
Bounded all-fan and thermal trajectory demonstrating the approved closed-loop behavior plus watchdog/abort record
Final no-override state, resolved 20-percent checkpoint, healthy RPM/temperature/alarms and post-log evidence
test_case.recovery: This case is itself a recovery operation, so a failed or unverified transition has no generic safe raw-command fallback. Stop, preserve monitoring/log evidence and invoke the platform-owner-approved thermal incident procedure, which may include an independently validated recovery mechanism or staffed shutdown. Never guess an alternate command, clear logs, power-cycle autonomously or retry.

source_conflict.reason: Master `0x30/0x21` and DeepSeek `0x30/0x30` auto commands conflict, and Master requires both dynamic algorithmic Auto control and a fixed 20-percent result without defining their relationship. The following Get row also lacks approved authority.

blocked.reason: The recovery objective and safe review contract are clear, but the necessary OEM and acceptance semantics require an engineering decision. The case stays Pending rather than adding a separate permanent BLOCKED classification.

pending.missing_evidence: Exact model/firmware-bound auto command and response; independent state query/decoder; approved meaning/tolerance/context for 20 percent; verified manual precondition; closed-loop evidence rule; monitoring/timeout/incident recovery; reviewed Script.
pending.responsible_owner: Platform BMC/thermal owner with firmware vendor and lab safety owner
pending.unblock_condition: Versioned approval and safe demonstration of the exact auto transition/readback plus resolution of fixed-20-percent versus dynamic-control acceptance on the intended firmware.
pending.execution_status: NOT EXECUTABLE; STATIC REVIEW ONLY; NO OEM COMMAND, FAN MODE CHANGE, SENSOR QUERY, LOG CLEAR, RESET, POWER OR DUT ACTION EXECUTED

external_authorities.title: Intelligent Platform Management Interface Specification v2.0 rev. 1.1
external_authorities.application: Defines manufacturer/product identification for interpreting OEM-specific functions but does not define either disputed fan auto-mode command.

external_authorities.title: DMTF Redfish Resource and Schema Guide 2025.3
external_authorities.application: Defines standard fan/sensor/status telemetry that can support independent monitoring; it does not define the OEM transition or make a fixed duty proof of Auto mode.

project_authority: Only the platform BMC/thermal owner and firmware-vendor specification can identify the correct transition/readback bytes and reconcile the fixed 20-percent statement with automatic feedback behavior. These missing semantics cannot be replaced with runtime placeholders.
